ועמ״א שכ״ח ומיהו י״ל בחובל לרפואה משום נטילת נשמה וא״כ בי״ט שני כה״ג ליכא ממ״נ והבן: והוי יודע דמילה דוחה צרעת כבסי׳ רס״ו בי״ד בספק בן ז׳ ח׳ ולא גזרו דוחה ממ״נ דהוי כמת וכמחתך בשר ואין שם בהרת כלל ואיסור דרבנן ליכא שם כמו בשבת ויש לשאול אם אותן שאין נימולין בשבת אם צרעת דוחה בהו כגון ב׳ ערלות ואנדרוגינוס וע׳ שבת קל״ה ותוס׳ שם וצ״ע: בסי׳ תקפ״ח בט״ז ה׳ דביום מפורש היתרא למילה בשבת אין כח ביד חז״ל לגזור דמלת ביום משמעות בין שיהיה שבת או י״ט וכמפורש היתרא כמו מועדו דאל״כ אימא ביום לרבות רק י״ט ש״מ דממשמעותיה נפיק ועתו״ש: מי שנולד מהול ספק בן ז׳ ח׳ להר״ב בי״ד רס״ו סי״א אין מוהלין בשבת וכ״ת ס״ס בשל תורה ובדרבנן חד ספק לקולא כבסי׳ ק״י שם הא בורכא דמה אמרת שמא בן ח׳ מחתך בשר ושרי מ״ה ואת״ל ז׳ שמא ערלה כבושה יש לו ושרי כמ״ש הרי״ף ובמ״א הביאותיו דמהול ספק הוא אדרבה יש ס״ס לאיסורא בדרבנן מיהת שמא בן ח׳ ולמה נתיר טילטול ושמא בן ז׳ ואין ערלה כבושה וכאמור: כל מ״ש המחבר בס״ה דאין מילתן דוחה שבת ה״ה י״ט דאין דוחה: הש״ך בי״ד רס״ב א׳ ב׳ הוכיח ממנחות ע״ב א׳ דמל תוך ז׳ צריך דיעבד למולו שנית מדדחי שבת הדא סובר דעשה דלולב אין דוחה לל״ת דשבת כרת ע׳ מהרש״א ומהרש״ל וס׳ הכריתות בסוגיא דיבמות ומשכחת לה בגווני טובא שא״א ליטול שם עכו״ם מבטל לה או פשוט אתרוג ברה״י ולולב ברה״י והדס ברה״י ורה״ר ביניהם וכר״י דאמר לולב צריך אגד ער״מ ומ״מ פרק ששי מה׳ לולב ותרנ״א מזה וא״כ בהכרח צריך שיוציא הלולב או ההדס לקרבן יחד ולעשות קשר בעניבה דלא כר״י או שאר קשרים או עכו״ם שנתן במתנה לישראל ולא מכוין לזכות בו עד שיוציא מרשותו ומבטלה דהוי שלו אף בי״ט א׳ ובפני עכו״ם מתירא שלא יהרגנו עסי׳ תרמ״ט ומשום דהוי בגווני רחיקא אמר דלא מהדא אלא בכ״ע פטור אף שאפשר לקיים בלא עקירת הלאו דטעה בדבר מצוה ואי״ה בס׳ זמנים יבואר עוד וגם בס׳ ש״ה וכאן אין להאריך:
cases.en_plain: (א) If you will see in Yoreh De'ah siman 266 s.k. 11 in Taz letter 8 he expanded; and Ra'avad here showed the source and ruled there that safek seven-day or eight-day even if his hair and nails did not finish — we circumcise in any case; and Taz wrote one should not be lenient — see there; and to be sharp and desecrate Shabbat for him — certainly one does not desecrate in safek seven-day or eight-day when his nails and hair did not finish — Eshel Avraham 15; and it implies d'rabbanan shvut they do through an Israelite too, like circumcising in any case even though muktzeh prohibition is d'rabbanan; and one could say muktzeh is lighter — behold there is a boracha of wounding in it, breaking, and even though breaking and blood is not needed — nevertheless d'rabbanan is forbidden in such a case (see siman 310 in Magen Avraham 16); and nevertheless permitted from d'rabbanan safek for leniency on account of milah mitzvah lest he be seven-day — likewise pikuach nefesh is great — they desecrate d'rabbanan: (ב) See in Even HaEzer part 2 Beit Shmuel letter 19: Shifra reads in seven even though between them only five months — likewise for Shabbat in such a case; and a woman who gives birth at nine months — likewise dispute there; and it is possible in milah there is no concern for Torah prohibition since in any case; and in d'rabbanan for leniency — requires study. And regarding safek eight-day and his hair did not finish, etc. — on the second day of Yom Tov in the Diaspora — requires study — Eshel Avraham 14 Yoreh De'ah 266 seif 8 tends to say safek overrides second day of Diaspora Yom Tov — all the more so here where there is in any case; and perhaps halacha is like Ra'avad there in s.k. 11 — see there; and see Rambam chapter 1 Laws of Milah halacha 15. And behold safek eight-day and his hair did not finish, etc., and born circumcised that needs hatafat dam brit — one can say it is breaking melacha, for blood is needed and like wounding for healing; and Or Sameach chapter 8 Laws of Wounding in wounding by way of revenge; however like R' Yehuda that from the time he removed his hand he is liable — nevertheless here it is needed for itself — see Kesubos daf for blood he needs; and in Tosafos there to see if she is a virgin — evidently all such breaking is breaking even though blood is not needed like breaking grain, etc.; and Magen Avraham 328; however one can say in wounding for healing on account of taking a soul; if so on second day Yom Tov in such a case there is no in any case — end: (ג) And know that milah overrides tzaraat — in siman 266 Yoreh De'ah in safek seven-day eight-day they did not decree it overrides in any case since it is like dead and like cutting flesh and there is no baheret at all and there is no d'rabbanan prohibition there like on Shabbat; and one may ask regarding those not circumcised on Shabbat whether tzaraat overrides for them, such as two arlot and androgynous — see Shabbos 135 and Tosafos there — requires study: (ד) In siman 488 Taz 5 that on an explicit day there is permission for milah on Shabbat — Chazal have no power to decree, for "on the day" implies whether Shabbat or Yom Tov; and if not, say "on the day" to include only Yom Tov — we learn from its implication; and explicit permission like its time — end: (ה) One born circumcised — safek seven-day eight-day — for Ra'avad Yoreh De'ah siman 266 s.k. 11 — they do not circumcise on Shabbat; and one could say end of siman 110 and in d'rabbanan one safek for leniency like siman 110 there — behold boracha of wounding — what will you say, perhaps eight-day — he cuts flesh and permitted melacha; and if you say seven-day — perhaps pressed foreskin he has and permitted as Rif wrote; and Magen Avraham brought you that circumcised is safek — on the contrary there is safek-safeka for prohibition in d'rabbanan; however perhaps eight-day — why permit muktzeh; and perhaps seven-day — no pressed foreskin as stated: (ו) All that Mechaber wrote in seif 5 that their milah does not override Shabbat — likewise Yom Tov, for it does not override: (ז) Shach Yoreh De'ah 262 seifim 1–2 proved from Menachos 72a that one circumcised within seven days needs after the fact to circumcise again since it pushes aside Shabbat; and it is difficult — nevertheless in nullification of positive commandment "on the eighth day you shall circumcise" unlike there where the essence of the mitzvah was fulfilled and the part of the mitzvah shortened at night is after the fact valid; and further there it is not explicit so much that plowing and reaping were needed for several matters, and it is reasonable similar to tamid as Tosafos wrote there; and also milah — thirteen covenants were cut and explicit permission in Torah; and see Shabbos 132a from "beloved is mitzvah at its time" — see there I was uncertain: one who transgressed and circumcised milah not at its time on Yom Tov — whether he receives lashes or not — from that which R' said Shabbos 133a Yom Tov positive commandment and negative commandment, and no positive commandment pushes aside positive commandment and negative commandment — one can say it pushes aside negative commandment in any case and valid for testimony and the like; and see Yerushalmi chapter Lulav HaGazul: first tanna's colleagues say R' Yossi's words (regarding taking lulav to reshut ha-rabbim on first day of Shabbat) that he is exempt, for positive commandment pushes aside negative commandment — R' Yossi said to them: not from this, etc. — see there; and colleagues hold he has no other lulav except this and it is in a non-Jew's hand and cannot take it except carrying to reshut ha-rabbim where positive commandment pushes aside negative commandment and only positive commandment of Shabbat — he is not liable for sin-offering specifically on negative commandment and not on positive commandment "which you shall not do" — Or Sameach chapter 1 halacha 6 from Laws of Unintentional Sin — see there; and R' Yossi who said to them "not from this" holds lulav positive commandment does not push aside Shabbat negative commandment where kares applies — see Maharsha and Maharshal and Sefer HaKeritut in sugya of Yevamos; and you find in many good cases where impossible to take there non-Jew cancels it, or plain etrog in reshut ha-yachid and lulav in reshut ha-yachid and hadas in reshut ha-yachid and reshut ha-rabbim between them; and like R' Yossi who said lulav requires binding — Or Sameach; and nevertheless chapter 6 Laws of Lulav and siman 491 from this; and if so perforce one must take out the lulav or hadas together to the sacrifice and make binding with tying unlike R' Yossi or other bindings; or non-Jew who gave as gift to Israel and does not intend to transfer ownership until he removes from his domain and cancels it though it is his even on first day of Yom Tov; and before a non-Jew he fears lest he kill him — see siman 449; and because it is a distant case they said not from this — rather according to all exempt even if possible to fulfill without uprooting the prohibition; mistaken in mitzvah matter — and if so in Sefer Zmanim more will be explained; and also in Sefer 305; and here one should not expand:

cases.he_html: בין השמשות. כתב ב"ח ובי"ד סי' רס"ו כתבתי דאם נולד שעה אחד מכ"ד קודם יציאת ג' כוכבים בינונים נימול ביום ו' ולאחר מכאן ספקא הוי ונמול ביו' א' ואף על גב דבסי' רס"א כתבתי דיש להחמיר לקבל שבת מסוף שעה כ"ב לענין מילה אינו כן עכ"ל הב"ח וצ"ע דהוא בעצמו פסק בי"ד ג' רביעי מיל קודם צ"ה הוי ב"ה וידוע דהם פחות מרביעית שעה כמ"ש סי' תנ"ט ואפשר ששגג לפום ריהטא וסבר שהוא ג' מיל והעיקר כמ"ש סי' רס"ו ס"ט בי"ד דמשתשקע החמה הוי ספק והיינו סוף השקיעה והוא ג' רביעי מיל כמש"ל סימן רס"א והוא לערך רביעית שעה קודם צ"ה ואם נולד קודם לכן מוהלין ביום ו' דהא אפי' לענין מלאכה דהוי איסור סקילה פסקינן הכי כמש"ל וכ"פ בס' מ"כ במ"ה מ"ב פ"ה וכ"כ רדב"ז ח"א רפ"ב ואם נולד בשבת שעה רביעית קודם הליל' כתב דנ"ל להלכה למולו בשבת אבל לא למעשה אא"כ יסכימו בזה רוב חכמי ישראל כי איני רוצה לסמוך על דעתי בענין חילול שבת החמורה ומשמע מדבריו דספק שלו לפי שנהגו כל ישראל במקומו לקבל שבת משתשקע החמה א"כ ה"ה לענין מ"ש אבל במדינתינו לפעמים אין מקבלין שבת עד סמוך לרביעית שעה לצ"ה כמ"ש סי' רס"א א"כ ה"ה לענין מילה יש לסמוך על זה למולו בשבת דהא כל גדולי הפוסקים סוברין כן:
cases.en_html: Twilight. Bach wrote, and in Yoreh De'ah siman 266 I wrote that if he was born one hour of the twenty-four before emergence of three medium stars — he is circumcised on the sixth day; and after that it is a safek and he is circumcised on the first day; and even though in siman 261 I wrote one should be stringent to accept Shabbat from the end of hour 22 — for milah it is not so — end of Bach; and requires study, for he himself ruled in Yoreh De'ah three-quarters of a mil before nightfall is twilight, and it is known they are less than a quarter-hour as written siman 459; and it is possible he erred in haste and thought it was three mil; and the essence is as written siman 266 s.k. 9 in Yoreh De'ah that from sunset it is a safek, meaning the end of sunset, and it is three-quarters of a mil as stated siman 261, and it is approximately a quarter-hour before nightfall; and if born before that — they circumcise on the sixth day, for even regarding melacha which is stoning prohibition we rule thus as stated above; and so in Sefer Machatzit HaShekel in Maggid Mishneh chapter 5; and so Radbaz part 1 chapter 282; and if born on Shabbat a quarter-hour before night — he wrote: and it appears to me for halacha to circumcise him on Shabbat, but not for practice unless most sages of Israel agree on this, for I do not wish to rely on my view in severe Shabbat desecration; and it is implied from his words that his safek is because they practiced in his place to accept Shabbat from sunset — if so, likewise regarding Motzei Shabbat; but in our country sometimes they do not accept Shabbat until close to a quarter-hour before nightfall as written siman 261 — if so, likewise regarding milah one may rely on this to circumcise him on Shabbat, for all the great poskim hold thus:

cases.en_html: Seif 63: eight-day-old if finished, etc. See Shabbos 135a, 136a, and chapter 8 Yevamos seifim 1–2; and behold Tosafos there and there wrote that Rashbag and Rabbanan dispute in two matters regarding definite eight-day: for Rabbanan a definite eight-day is a non-viable infant and does not leave non-viable status until twenty years; for R' Avahu in safek and stam velados he holds it is certainly viable, for we follow majority of women as written there 37a "if you will say," etc.; and for Rashbag in both it is safek non-viable until thirty days, and after thirty days it is certainly a viable infant in both, for the sugya of Yevamos 40 disputes regarding definite eight-day, and in sugya of Shabbos and in the first chapter of Moed Katan 40 they dispute in safek as written; and so all poskim; and Ramban wrote in Yevamos there that both for Rabbanan and Rashbag there is no distinction at all whether finished or not; and so Maggid Mishneh there and there did not mention finished at all except R' Yehuda alone regarding definite eight-day, which for Rashbag is safek specifically regarding finished hair — if not finished it is definite non-viable, for otherwise definite non-viable that would be like a stone for Rashbag you would not find; and R' Yehuda holds that with finished hair he exits from definite status but not from safek status, and his time is unknown to R' Yehuda when he exits safek status; and R' Yehuda's view is seven months and one-third; and so Rivash siman 446 — except he wrote for R' Yehuda with finished hair he is definite viable infant and there is no practical difference for law, for halacha is not like R' Yehuda as written in Yevamos "like whom is R' Yehuda," etc.; and Rivash also wrote for Rabbanan in safek he is not viable until finished hair; and thereby Ramban's words appear correct that there is no distinction as stated, and practical difference for wife of kohen we rely on Rabbanan as written 37a regarding wife of kohen since impossible, etc.; and in Shabbos 136a Abbaye said "he cried out and died" — for all agree not viable; and if so in crying out for all non-viable, and even kohen's wife performs chalitzah; and likewise ill according to some commentators as Rabbenu Yonah and Rosh wrote — except Rabbeinu Alfas omitted this of Abbaye, and so Rambam and Shulchan Aruch; and they ruled all safek nine-day kohen's wife does not perform chalitzah, for they hold Rava who said "if kohen's wife," etc., and he did not distinguish between crying out — disputes Abbaye; and halacha like Rava; and in completion of his months certainly, such as he had relations and separated — even Rashbag agrees immediately viable as written in Shabbos there; and in Niddah 44b "completion of his months" — for Rambam specifically nine complete months; and so in Shulchan Aruch as written 38a–b: Shmuel said "a woman," etc., "as early chasidim said," Mar Zutra said, etc., "Mar Zutra even," etc. — all hold thus; and so sugya Yevamos 36a, 40 — thus even though Ramban disputes and explains like R' Yehuda in Niddah there except Ritva explains nature changed now and we see he is viable; and women give birth even day one of ninth month; and so Bach in Even HaEzer siman 156 seif 4; and as Tosafos wrote in Bechoros nature changed now that we say in Bechoros 19b cow and donkey, etc. — found in completion of his months for all he is viable; and definite eight-day or safek for Rashbag until thirty days — safek only definite eight-day without finished hair is definite non-viable; and if he waited thirty days — for all certainly viable whether eight-day or safek whether finished or not; and in Shabbos 136a halacha was decided like Rashbag; and commentators explain even regarding definite eight-day for all halacha is like him except for wife of kohen we rely on Rabbanan who hold definite viable whether finished or not; but for eight-day always chalitzah; and thus Ramban in Yevamos briefly: completion of his months — proper offspring; not complete and not finished hair — complete non-viable; finished hair — safek unknown whether complete whether finished or not — safek; waited thirty days according to all — forever like complete bridegroom for all; and regarding wife of kohen, etc., as stated; and see in Maggid Mishneh chapter 1 Laws of Yibum he brought his words; but Rambam seized another method: in chapter 1 Laws of Milah he wrote eight-day-old if complete in hair and nails — he is complete offspring; seven-day-old merely delayed and permitted to move and not like a stone and circumcise on Shabbat; if incomplete — this is definite eight-day and like a stone forbidden to move; and nevertheless if he waited — like other born for all that all who waited thirty days is not non-viable; seven-day if born complete — viable and circumcise on Shabbat; safek seven safek eight — circumcise on Shabbat in any case, etc.; and he ruled in both leniently like R' Yehuda and Rashbag; and what he wrote seven-day complete — see Taz and Beit Yosef siman 266; but in other places he did not mention R' Yehuda at all; and also in other matters his words appear contradictory: chapter 2 Laws of Murder he wrote born less than nine months — one who kills him exempt until waited thirty days; chapter 1 Laws of Yibum if not known completion of months until thirty days — safek; if waited thirty days — viable and exempt, etc.; chapter 1 Laws of Festivities non-viable infants — no mourning; all who did not wait thirty days — non-viable; if not known completion of months eight-day even after thirty days — non-viable and no, etc.; chapter 1 Laws of Inheritance even minor day-old without completion of months — inherits and bequeaths since lived one hour: the matter is as written chapter 1 Laws of Yibum from Torah if offspring emerged alive to the world's air even died hour born — exempt, etc.; but from rabbinic law until known certainly completion of months or waited thirty days; if not — safek and needs chalitzah from rabbinic law; therefore in inheritance law they established Torah law, for monetary law leniency for one stringency for other; and in other places he explains like Rashbag except in mourning where we hold halacha like lenient in mourning — certainly like Rabbanan that even after thirty days non-viable; and in milah since stringency in general that in any case they circumcise only on account of muktzeh he ruled like R' Yehuda and Rashbag leniently and holds R' Yehuda's words were stated only regarding milah as written in Yevamos there; therefore he did not mention his words elsewhere and explains like Rashbag even in murder; and see Maggid Mishneh chapter 1 Laws of Yibum and in Beit Yosef Choshen Mishpat siman 276; and Rambam learned from what we say regarding wife of kohen she does not perform chalitzah and we permit Torah prohibition — it would have been more reasonable to permit chalitzah for her husband who is d'rabbanan; and he learned from this that from Torah law chalitzah not needed; and see in Tosafos there; and in Shulchan Aruch he ruled like Rambam in Choshen Mishpat siman 276 explains like his words in Laws of Inheritance; and in Even HaEzer siman 156 seif 4 copied Rambam's words chapter 1 Laws of Yibum; and in Shulchan Aruch Yoreh De'ah siman 374 seif 8 wrote also like Rambam chapter 1 there and added until thirty days even finished hair and nails, etc. — and this is Ramban's words Yoreh De'ah there and as his method as stated; and gemara's question "from where do we circumcise" — how do we circumcise with finished hair as written in Yevamos; and so Rif there; and Rav Adda needed to force thus; but we who hold like the resolution in Yevamos — and thus he wrote here "even if safek," etc.; and so Beit Yosef siman 266; but Bach wrote there like Rambam and Tur that even without finished hair circumcise in any case in safek eight-day; and with finished hair even definite eight-day we rely on R' Yehuda; but what is written siman 310 seif 7 that with finished hair whether safek or definite desecrate Shabbat for him — requires study; and perhaps because safek nefashot to be lenient we rely on R' Yehuda; except if so in safek even without finished hair should have said desecrate like wife of kohen we rely on Rabbanan; and one could say he holds like Rivash that without finished hair even Rabbanan agree; מלין אותו בשבת ממ"נ כו' ופסק בשניהם לקולא כרבי וכרשב"ג ומ"ש בן ז' שלם כ' דל"ד וע' בטי"ד וב"י סי' רס"ו. אבל בשאר מקומות לא הזכיר כלל הא דרבי וג"כ בשאר דברים נראין כסותרין דבריו שבפ"ב מה' רוצח כ' דנולד יום ה"ז נפל אם אינו ידוע שכלו חדשיו בן שמנה אף לאחר ל' יום ה"ז נפל ואין כו'. ובפ"א מה' נחלות כ' אפי' קטן בן יומו ולא כלו חדשיו ה"ז נוחל ומנחיל הואיל וחי שעה אחת: והענין הוא כמ"ש בפ"א מה' יבום מן התורה אם יצא הולד חי לאויר העולם אפי' מת בשעה שנולד פטורה כו' אבל מד"ס עד שיודע בודאי שכלו חדשיו או שישהה שלשים יום ואם לאו ה"ז ספק וצריכה חליצה מד"ס לכן בדין נחלות אוקמוהו אדין תורה דבדיני ממונות קולא לזה וחומרא לזה ובשאר מקומות פ' כרשב"ג רק באבל דקי"ל הלכה כדברי המיקל באבל פ' בודאי כרבנן דאף לאחר ל' יום הרי זה נפל ובמילה כיון דחומרא בעלמא דממ"נ מלין אותו רק משום טלטול פסק כדברי רבי ורשב"ג לקולא וס"ל דדברי רבי לא אתמר אלא לענין מילה כמ"ש ביבמות שם ולכן לא הזכיר דבריו בשאר מקומות ופ' כרשב"ג אף ברוצח וע' מ"מ פ"א מה' יבום ובב"י ח"מ סי' רע"ו ולמד הרמב"ם מדאמרינן באשת כהן דאינה חולצת ושרינן איסורא דאורייתא ויותר היה נראה להתיר חליצה לבעלה שהוא דרבנן ולמד מזה שמדין תורה א"צ חליצה וע' בתוס' שם ובש"ע פסק כהרמב"ם שבח"מ סי' רע"ו פ' שם כדבריו בהל' נחלות ובא"ע סי' קנ"ו ס"ד העתיק דברי רמב"ם בפ"א מהל' יבום ובש"ע י"ד סי' שע"ד ס"ח כ' ג"כ כדברי הרמב"ם פ"א שם והוסיף שעד ל' יום אפי' גמרו שערו וצפרניו כו' והוא מדברי הרמב"ן יטי"ד שם וכשיטתו כנ"ל וענ"י ביבמות שם וט"ס שם וגם הרמב"ם יודה בזה כנ"ל אבל במילה כ' שדעת הרי"ף ורא"ש שלא כתב הא דרב אדא דאמר מלין אותו ממה נפשך שמע מינה דלא סבירא ליה הא דרב אדא וקושיית הגמ' מימהל היכי מהלינן בשגמרו דמש"ה מהלינן כמ"ש ביבמות וכ"כ הרי"ף שם ורב אדא הוא דאצטריך לדחוקי כך אבל אנן דס"ל כאוקימתא דיבמות וז"ש כאן אפי' אם הוא ספק כו' וכ"כ בי"ד סי' רס"ו אבל ב"ה כ' שם כדעת הרמב"ם וטור דאפי' לא גמרו מלין אותו ממ"נ בספק בן ח' ובגמרו אפי' ודאי בן ח' סמכינן ארבי אבל מ"ש בסי' ש"ל ס"ז דבגמרו בין ספק בין ודאי מחללין עליו שבת צ"ע ואפשר משום דספק נפשות להקל וסמכינן ארבי אלא דא"כ בספק אפי' לא גמרו הל"ל דמחללין כמו באשת כהן דסמכינן ארבנן וא"ל דס"ל כדעת הריב"ש דבלא גמרו אף רבנן מודו דא"כ הל"ל באשת כהן ג"כ דוקא גמרו וע' ספ"ק דערכין דאף על הספק מחללין וע' ר"ן פ' בתרא דיומא ומ"ש מ"א שם משום דאיכא ריעותא דלא גמרו מש"ה אין מחללין לדעת הרמב"ן וכ"פ בש"ע א"ה סי' קס"ד ס"ז דבאשת כהן לעולם אין חולצת ולא חילק בין גמרו או לא ה"ה כאן ואף לרשב"ג כיון דספק הוא מחללין כנ"ל ובספק נפשות מקילינן יותר מבכ"מ. וגם דברי הטוא"ה וב"ה בסי' קנ"ו ס"ד צ"ע דכ' דאפי' בסתם ולדות אין פוטר עד שיהיה בן שלשים יום וגמרו שערו וצפרניו דזהו דלא כחד ואף לדעת התו' שכ' ביבמות שם ובשבת שם דרבי ורשב"ג ל"פ אלא דשניהם בעינן ל' יום וגמרו היינו בודאי בן ח' אבל בספק כ' דא"צ וע"ש בתו' דשבת ד"ה מימהל. וא"ת היכי פשיט כו' וי"ל דא"כ הל"ל כו' ומדנקט רשב"ג ש"מ דבסתם כו':
cases.en_plain: Seif 63: eight-day-old if finished, etc. See Shabbos 135a, 136a, and chapter 8 Yevamos seifim 1–2; and behold Tosafos there and there wrote that Rashbag and Rabbanan dispute in two matters regarding definite eight-day: for Rabbanan a definite eight-day is a non-viable infant and does not leave non-viable status until twenty years; for R' Avahu in safek and stam velados he holds it is certainly viable, for we follow majority of women as written there 37a "if you will say," etc.; and for Rashbag in both it is safek non-viable until thirty days, and after thirty days it is certainly a viable infant in both, for the sugya of Yevamos 40 disputes regarding definite eight-day, and in sugya of Shabbos and in the first chapter of Moed Katan 40 they dispute in safek as written; and so all poskim; and Ramban wrote in Yevamos there that both for Rabbanan and Rashbag there is no distinction at all whether finished or not; and so Maggid Mishneh there and there did not mention finished at all except R' Yehuda alone regarding definite eight-day, which for Rashbag is safek specifically regarding finished hair — if not finished it is definite non-viable, for otherwise definite non-viable that would be like a stone for Rashbag you would not find; and R' Yehuda holds that with finished hair he exits from definite status but not from safek status, and his time is unknown to R' Yehuda when he exits safek status; and R' Yehuda's view is seven months and one-third; and so Rivash siman 446 — except he wrote for R' Yehuda with finished hair he is definite viable infant and there is no practical difference for law, for halacha is not like R' Yehuda as written in Yevamos "like whom is R' Yehuda," etc.; and Rivash also wrote for Rabbanan in safek he is not viable until finished hair; and thereby Ramban's words appear correct that there is no distinction as stated, and practical difference for wife of kohen we rely on Rabbanan as written 37a regarding wife of kohen since impossible, etc.; and in Shabbos 136a Abbaye said "he cried out and died" — for all agree not viable; and if so in crying out for all non-viable, and even kohen's wife performs chalitzah; and likewise ill according to some commentators as Rabbenu Yonah and Rosh wrote — except Rabbeinu Alfas omitted this of Abbaye, and so Rambam and Shulchan Aruch; and they ruled all safek nine-day kohen's wife does not perform chalitzah, for they hold Rava who said "if kohen's wife," etc., and he did not distinguish between crying out — disputes Abbaye; and halacha like Rava; and in completion of his months certainly, such as he had relations and separated — even Rashbag agrees immediately viable as written in Shabbos there; and in Niddah 44b "completion of his months" — for Rambam specifically nine complete months; and so in Shulchan Aruch as written 38a–b: Shmuel said "a woman," etc., "as early chasidim said," Mar Zutra said, etc., "Mar Zutra even," etc. — all hold thus; and so sugya Yevamos 36a, 40 — thus even though Ramban disputes and explains like R' Yehuda in Niddah there except Ritva explains nature changed now and we see he is viable; and definite eight-day or safek for Rashbag until thirty days — safek only definite eight-day without finished hair is definite non-viable; and if he waited thirty days — for all certainly viable whether eight-day or safek whether finished or not;
